summary: Phase 149O.16.2 -- Publication Coordinator Timestamp Compatibility Independent Verification: independently determined whether 149O.16.1 correctly repaired the Python 3.9/3.10 compatibility defect (149O.12B-Obs-PY39-1) in pcae.governance.publication.coordinator._parse_timestamp. Ran the required initial inspection and confirmed baseline: repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.16.1 completed/complete, HMRC-001 v1.0 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- CONFORMS, HATP production NOT READY, runtime Observed/observe/unavailable. Reconstructed the production diff independently from Git history (git diff 44c3d024 HEAD -- src/pcae/): exactly one file (coordinator.py), exactly one removed line (bare fromisoformat(value)) and two added code lines (terminal-Z normalization + fromisoformat(text)), classified Z_SUFFIX_COMPATIBILITY, UNRELATED=0. Reconstructed the pre-repair source directly via git show 44c3d024:... (bare fromisoformat, no endswith/Z handling) rather than trusting 149O.16.1's own report. Confirmed the repaired source via inspect.getsource matches the safe precedent rollback_approval_evidence._parse_iso_timestamp's identical normalization line. CORRECTION TO 149O.16.1: that phase's report stated no Python 3.9/3.10 interpreter was available locally (only 3.14.5); this phase independently reconfirmed the interpreter and found the repository's own .venv is actually CPython 3.9.6 (pyvenv.cfg home=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin) -- the prior claim was an artifact of an interactive shell's PATH resolving a bare `python3` to Homebrew's 3.14 first, not a fact about the machine (confirmed: /usr/bin/python3 and .venv/bin/python are both 3.9.6; python3.10 is not installed anywhere on this machine). All of this phase's tests, and the full regression sweep, therefore ran under genuine CPython 3.9.6 -- real empirical Python 3.9 coverage, not simulated/structural reasoning; Python 3.10 remains NOT EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT (no interpreter available). Authored a new, independently-designed 33-test file (tests/test_phase_149o_16_2_publication_timestamp_compatibility_independent_verification.py) importing none of the three historical monkeypatch fixtures, covering: production-diff exactness and hunk classification via git subprocess calls; pre-repair source reconstruction from git show; repaired-source structural checks; terminal-Z acceptance; Z/+00:00 exact instant equivalence; fractional-Z preservation; non-UTC-offset non-regression (no forced UTC conversion); +00:00 non-regression (no double suffix); lowercase-z rejection; Z-with-trailing-garbage rejection; interior-Z rejection; malformed-input rejection; naive-timestamp UTC coercion unchanged; uniform ValueError error-mapping; a direct no-monkeypatch call proving _coordinator._parse_timestamp is the real function; a real PublicationCoordinator.authorize->execute run with Z-suffixed built_at/invoked_at (no monkeypatch); the same path with +00:00 timestamps proving no authority-semantic change for already-accepted input; and -- independently discovered, not merely restated -- that pcae.core.rollback_approval_evidence.create_rollback_approval_decision (the sole real production entry point for CHGR Decision creation) always builds its built_at via chgr_envelope.chgr_timestamp(...), which always emits a Z-suffixed string, meaning every real call to this function was broken pre-repair on Python 3.9/3.10, not merely a contrived test input; exercised this end-to-end with no monkeypatch through to a real create_rollback_approval_binding (AG3 RAE Binding) call, confirming binding.governance_record_reference == the created Decision ref. Verified scope boundaries via git diff --stat against the phase-start commit: all seven contracts (HSCE-001, HATP-001, RAE-001, RWMPC-001, PBPA-001, PBPC-001, HMRC-001) byte-unchanged; hatp_signing_ceremony.py, hatp_ag_authority.py, hatp_signed_evidence.py, hatp_evidence_store.py, agent.py, commands/agent.py all byte-unchanged; no permission_broker-named file touched; no 'cutover' string introduced; no new production files added. NON-BLOCKING FINDING (independently discovered, not documented by 149O.16.1): on this repository's actual CPython 3.9.6 interpreter, datetime.fromisoformat silently ignores any single stray character immediately preceding an otherwise-valid +00:00 offset (e.g. '...56X+00:00' parses successfully); because the repair unconditionally strips exactly one trailing 'Z', a malformed double-Z input ('...56ZZ') normalizes to '...56Z+00:00', which this same stdlib quirk then accepts -- whereas the pre-repair bare fromisoformat('...56ZZ') call correctly raised ValueError. Confirmed via direct comparison that this is NOT specific to 149O.16.1's repair: rollback_approval_evidence._parse_iso_timestamp, the exact 'safe precedent' this repair mirrors, exhibits the identical behavior for the identical input, and has done so since before this phase (untouched by 149O.16.1); also confirmed it does not reproduce on Python 3.14 (fromisoformat there correctly rejects both forms), proving it is a Python-3.9-only CPython stdlib interaction, not a logic defect in either module's normalization line. Disposed as pre-existing, repository-wide, non-blocking, out of scope for a narrow follow-up repair to 149O.16.1 specifically (fixing coordinator.py alone would create the two functions' first behavioral divergence from their shared precedent). Ran targeted regression across HATP signing ceremony + 149O.12B/12C/13/15/16 + 149O.16.1's own file: 294 passed, 2 failed. Both failures independently confirmed pre-existing and unrelated by reproducing them identically with this phase's new test file stashed out (git stash -u): (1) test_phase_149o_13_...py's own sys.version_info >= (3,11) assumption, now genuinely false under the real 3.9.6 .venv -- a pre-existing test fragility this phase's interpreter discovery unmasked, not a repair defect; (2) test_phase_149o_16_...py's 'no src/pcae/ change since 149O.16's own phase-entry commit' assertion, now false because 149O.16.1 (a later, separate phase) legitimately changed coordinator.py afterward -- expected staleness of a phase-scoped assertion. Ran a broader publication/rollback-approval-evidence/CHGR/report-trust sweep (1400+ tests): 1400 passed, 1 skipped, 6 failed, all six independently confirmed pre-existing via the same git-stash technique (two wheel-packaging checks, four tests in a known, pre-existing B-149M-2-class CHGR/publication-receipt forgery finding unrelated to timestamp parsing). Ran the full repository-wide Fast Green (pytest -m fast_green): 5177 passed, 2 failed (the same two pre-existing failures above), 1 skipped -- zero new failures. Authored the phase document, docs/PHASE_149O_16_2_PUBLICATION_COORDINATOR_TIMESTAMP_COMPATIBILITY_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md, covering baseline, corrected interpreter finding, pre/post-repair source reconstruction, production diff, safe precedent, direct parser verification table, real CHGR/RAE path verification, historical monkeypatch inventory, updated historical test audit, regression results with pre-existing-failure attribution, the non-blocking fromisoformat quirk finding with its own precedent-parity proof, scope boundaries, verification verdict, and finding disposition. VERDICT: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- PUBLICATION COORDINATOR TIMESTAMP COMPATIBILITY REPAIR CONFORMS. 149O.12B-Obs-PY39-1: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED RESOLVED. HMRC-001 v1.0 remains byte-unchanged and VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- CONFORMS. HSCE-001/HATP-001/RAE-001/PB contracts remain byte-unchanged. No HMRC-001 implementation was started. B-149O-1..4 remain INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AT HATP-GATED AUTHORITY BOUNDARY -- SYSTEM EXECUTION CLOSURE DEFERRED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Full detail in docs/PHASE_149O_16_2_PUBLICATION_COORDINATOR_TIMESTAMP_COMPATIBILITY_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md. Recommended next phase: 149O.17 -- HATP Mandatory Production Consumption Implementation Plan.
